svg.title: TechFlow Customer Success Digital FTE — Production
svg.desc: Production multi-channel customer support: customers enter through the Next.js web form, Gmail or WhatsApp. FastAPI intake persists tickets in PostgreSQL and publishes Kafka events. A separate worker runs triage, support and escalation agents and delivers replies through Gmail or Twilio. Includes production metrics, container builds, Kubernetes and Docker Compose definitions, and production test suites.

Customer
g.desc: Person requesting TechFlow support through the web form, email or WhatsApp.. Purpose: Show where the customer joins the application and where support replies are addressed.. How it works: The customer submits the Next.js support form, sends a support email through Gmail, or sends a WhatsApp message through Twilio. The existing channel adapters and API handle these requests. Email and web-form answers use Gmail; WhatsApp answers use Twilio.. Inputs: Support question; Selected communication channel. Outputs: Web form request; Support email; WhatsApp support message. Dependencies: Next.js support form; Gmail API; Twilio WhatsApp API. Evidence: production/web-form/app/page.tsx: SupportPage, handleSubmit; production/channels/web_form_handler.py: submit_support_form; production/channels/gmail_handler.py: get_message, poll_new_emails, send_reply; production/channels/whatsapp_handler.py: process_webhook, poll_new_messages, send_message; production/workers/message_processor.py: deliver_response. Uncertainty: Email and WhatsApp initiation are inferred from the customer-facing incoming-message contracts.. Source: production/web-form/app/page.tsx

g.title: Next.js support form
g.desc: React client page validates support requests, submits JSON and displays the returned ticket ID.. Purpose: React client page validates support requests, submits JSON and displays the returned ticket ID.. How it works: SupportPage manages local form state and POSTs to /support/submit using NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL. The Next.js build uses standalone output.. Inputs: Support request fields. Outputs: Ticket confirmation or validation error. Dependencies: FastAPI application. Evidence: production/web-form/app/page.tsx: SupportPage, validate, handleSubmit; production/web-form/package.json: Next.js 16.2.3, React 19.2.4; production/web-form/next.config.ts: output standalone. Uncertainty: The inspected page implements submission and confirmation; API ticket retrieval is not wired into this UI.. Source: production/web-form/app/page.tsx

g.title: FastAPI application
g.desc: Uvicorn entry point hosts support, webhook, CRM lookup, statistics and health routes.. Purpose: Uvicorn entry point hosts support, webhook, CRM lookup, statistics and health routes.. How it works: Lifespan opens a database pool, initializes Gmail watch and starts two daemon polling threads. The application mounts the support router and registers the remaining HTTP routes.. Evidence: production/api/main.py: app, lifespan, app.include_router; production/Dockerfile: uvicorn api.main:app. Source: production/api/main.py

g.aria-label: Support submission and ticket API, API
g.title: Support submission and ticket API
g.desc: Validates support submissions and exposes ticket status with conversation messages.. Purpose: Validates support submissions and exposes ticket status with conversation messages.. How it works: POST /support/submit resolves customer and conversation, creates a ticket, stores the inbound message and publishes fte.tickets.incoming. GET /support/ticket/{ticket_id} reads ticket history.. Inputs: Validated support request or ticket ID. Outputs: Ticket ID or ticket status and messages. Dependencies: Database access layer; Kafka client. Evidence: production/channels/web_form_handler.py: SupportFormSubmission, submit_support_form, get_ticket_status. Source: production/channels/web_form_handler.py

g.aria-label: CRM lookup and statistics API, API
g.title: CRM lookup and statistics API
g.desc: Serves customer, ticket, conversation, system statistics and per-channel metrics queries.. Purpose: Serves customer, ticket, conversation, system statistics and per-channel metrics queries.. How it works: GET /admin/customers, /admin/tickets, /admin/tickets/{ticket_id}, /customers/lookup, /conversations/{conversation_id}, /stats and /metrics/channels execute database queries.. Evidence: production/api/main.py: list_all_customers, list_all_tickets, get_admin_ticket_detail; production/api/main.py: lookup_customer, get_conversation, stats, get_channel_metrics. Uncertainty: No dashboard frontend is evidenced by the inspected support page.. Source: production/api/main.py

g.aria-label: Gmail and WhatsApp polling threads, Job
g.title: Gmail and WhatsApp polling threads
g.desc: Background loops pull inbound mail and WhatsApp messages into the CRM.. Purpose: Background loops pull inbound mail and WhatsApp messages into the CRM.. How it works: _start_polling creates separate event loops in daemon threads, running each poll every 30 seconds. Each cycle stores customer, conversation, ticket and message records and publishes the channel inbound topic.. Evidence: production/api/main.py: _start_polling, _gmail_poll_once, _whatsapp_poll_once. Uncertainty: Every API process starts these threads; cross-replica polling coordination is not established by this file.. Source: production/api/main.py

g.title: Gmail channel adapter
g.desc: Reads and normalizes Gmail messages, requests an inbox watch and sends MIME replies.. Purpose: Reads and normalizes Gmail messages, requests an inbox watch and sends MIME replies.. How it works: GmailHandler builds the Gmail v1 client from configured local OAuth files. Polling lists unread support-labeled messages; notification processing reads Gmail history. send_reply can preserve a thread ID.. Evidence: production/channels/gmail_handler.py: GmailHandler.authenticate, start_watch; production/channels/gmail_handler.py: poll_new_emails, process_notification, send_reply. Source: production/channels/gmail_handler.py

g.title: Twilio WhatsApp channel adapter
g.desc: Normalizes WhatsApp webhooks, polls inbound Twilio messages and sends replies.. Purpose: Normalizes WhatsApp webhooks, polls inbound Twilio messages and sends replies.. How it works: WhatsAppHandler lazily constructs a Twilio REST client, validates signatures when configured and persists a polling timestamp in PostgreSQL channel_configs. send_message calls Twilio messages.create.. Evidence: production/channels/whatsapp_handler.py: WhatsAppHandler, validate_webhook, process_webhook; production/channels/whatsapp_handler.py: poll_new_messages, _load_checkpoint, _save_checkpoint, send_message. Uncertainty: Signature validation is skipped when authentication configuration is absent.. Source: production/channels/whatsapp_handler.py

g.title: Shared Kafka publishing client
g.desc: Publishes intake events using a synchronous kafka-python producer wrapped for async callers.. Purpose: Publishes intake events using a synchronous kafka-python producer wrapped for async callers.. How it works: FTEKafkaProducer shares one producer across event loops and runs send/acknowledgement in asyncio.to_thread. publish_to_kafka is the channel wrapper. Failed or unavailable publishing returns without blocking persisted intake.. Evidence: production/kafka_client.py: FTEKafkaProducer.get_instance, publish, _sync_send, TOPICS; production/channels/web_form_handler.py: publish_to_kafka. Uncertainty: TOPICS declares nine topics, including outbound, escalation, metrics and DLQ names; active publishers for those auxiliary topics were not evidenced.. Source: production/kafka_client.py

g.aria-label: Incoming ticket and channel topics, Queue
g.title: Incoming ticket and channel topics
g.desc: Kafka topic set carrying persisted intake records to the message processor.. Purpose: Kafka topic set carrying persisted intake records to the message processor.. How it works: The worker subscribes to fte.tickets.incoming plus email, WhatsApp and webform inbound topics. Web submission and webhooks use the unified topic; API pollers publish channel-specific email and WhatsApp events.. Evidence: production/kafka_client.py: TOPICS; production/workers/message_processor.py: run_kafka_consumer; production/api/main.py: _gmail_poll_once, _whatsapp_poll_once, gmail_webhook, whatsapp_webhook; production/channels/web_form_handler.py: submit_support_form. Uncertainty: The webform-specific inbound topic is declared and subscribed; inspected web submissions publish the unified topic instead.. Source: production/kafka_client.py

g.title: Kafka broker
g.desc: Broker deployment supplies the event transport used by intake and the worker.. Purpose: Broker deployment supplies the event transport used by intake and the worker.. How it works: Kubernetes declares one wurstmeister Kafka replica, a service on 9092, ZooKeeper connection and automatic topic creation. Docker Compose declares a Confluent Kafka broker.. Evidence: production/k8s/04-kafka.yaml: kafka Deployment, Service, KAFKA_ZOOKEEPER_CONNECT; production/docker-compose.yml: kafka service. Source: production/k8s/04-kafka.yaml

g.aria-label: Message processor and reply delivery, Service
g.title: Message processor and reply delivery
g.desc: Separate process consumes intake records, runs the agent flow and delivers stored replies.. Purpose: Separate process consumes intake records, runs the agent flow and delivers stored replies.. How it works: process_message calls Runner.run(triage_agent), retrieves the outbound response stored for the ticket, delivers via Gmail or Twilio and records latency. Web-form replies are emailed when an address is available.. Evidence: production/workers/message_processor.py: main, run_kafka_consumer, process_message; production/workers/message_processor.py: _get_stored_agent_response, deliver_response, _record_metrics; production/k8s/06-deployment-worker.yaml: workers/message_processor.py. Uncertainty: Automatic fallback to database polling depends on an exception escaping run_kafka_consumer; some consumer failures are caught or return normally.; Channel delivery errors are logged; no durable retry or DLQ write is evidenced by this worker.. Source: production/workers/message_processor.py

g.title: Open-ticket polling mode
g.desc: Alternative worker intake reads open tickets from PostgreSQL.. Purpose: Alternative worker intake reads open tickets from PostgreSQL.. How it works: run_db_poller selects up to ten open tickets, retrieves the latest inbound message, marks each ticket in_progress and calls process_message. The default polling interval is five seconds.. Evidence: production/workers/message_processor.py: run_db_poller, main. Uncertainty: PROCESSOR_MODE selects polling explicitly; automatic fallback is conditional. Ticket selection and status updates are separate operations.. Source: production/workers/message_processor.py

g.title: Triage agent
g.desc: Entry agent retrieves customer context, records sentiment and chooses support or escalation.. Purpose: Entry agent retrieves customer context, records sentiment and chooses support or escalation.. How it works: The OpenAI Agents SDK definition configures three tools, an input guardrail and handoffs to the support and escalation agents. The worker supplies the existing intake ticket ID.. Inputs: Inbound message context and existing ticket ID. Outputs: Support or escalation handoff. Dependencies: Agent tools; Guardrails; Configured LLM. Evidence: production/agent/customer_success_agent.py: triage_agent, handoff_to_support, handoff_to_escalation; production/workers/message_processor.py: process_message. Chart: Configured tool registrations per runtime agent. Independent categories; bars are not connected. Triage: 3 tools; Support: 5 tools; Escalation: 3 tools. Unit: tools. Evidence: production/agent/customer_success_agent.py: count the tools list in triage_agent, support_agent and escalation_agent (shared tools counted per agent).. Source: production/agent/customer_success_agent.py

g.title: Support agent
g.desc: Product-support specialist retrieves documentation and stores ticket replies.. Purpose: Product-support specialist retrieves documentation and stores ticket replies.. How it works: Five registered tools cover KB search, send_response and ticket operations. The definition adds an output guardrail and a handoff to escalation for unsupported requests.. Evidence: production/agent/customer_success_agent.py: support_agent, handoff_from_support_to_escalation. Source: production/agent/customer_success_agent.py

g.title: Escalation agent
g.desc: Specialist records requests for human support and can store a customer reply.. Purpose: Specialist records requests for human support and can store a customer reply.. How it works: Three configured tools are escalate_to_human, update_ticket_status and send_response. create_escalation persists the escalation and updates the ticket.. Evidence: production/agent/customer_success_agent.py: escalation_agent; production/agent/tools.py: escalate_to_human; production/database/queries.py: create_escalation. Uncertainty: No external human-support notification or assignment integration is evidenced; the tool creates CRM records.. Source: production/agent/customer_success_agent.py

g.title: Input and output guardrails
g.desc: Checks triage input and support output with keyword rules followed by an LLM check.. Purpose: Checks triage input and support output with keyword rules followed by an LLM check.. How it works: check_input_safety and check_output_quality return Agents SDK tripwire results. Guardrail runners use the configured model provider; exceptions allow processing to continue.. Evidence: production/agent/guardrails.py: check_input_safety, check_output_quality, _get_model_config. Uncertainty: Checks fail open on LLM errors. Escalation has no configured guardrail. Support output checks do not establish that earlier tool side effects were prevented.. Source: production/agent/guardrails.py

g.title: CRM and knowledge-base tools
g.desc: Nine function tools support customer history, sentiment, tickets, documentation search, stored responses and escalations.. Purpose: Nine function tools support customer history, sentiment, tickets, documentation search, stored responses and escalations.. How it works: Tools use asyncpg pools or database helper functions. KB search matches title/content with ILIKE. send_response stores an outbound message and sets the ticket to responded; channel delivery is performed later by the worker.. Evidence: production/agent/tools.py: get_customer_history, record_sentiment, create_ticket; production/agent/tools.py: search_knowledge_base, send_response, get_ticket, update_ticket_status, search_tickets; production/agent/tools.py: escalate_to_human. Uncertainty: send_response persists the reply; the message worker performs external channel delivery.. Source: production/agent/tools.py

g.title: Fallback channel formatting
g.desc: Formats fallback responses and error apologies for email, WhatsApp and web form.. Purpose: Formats fallback responses and error apologies for email, WhatsApp and web form.. How it works: format_for_channel dispatches to per-channel helpers. The message processor uses it for final_output fallback and processing-error apologies.. Evidence: production/agent/formatters.py: format_for_channel; production/workers/message_processor.py: process_message, _send_error_apology. Uncertainty: The ordinary stored-response delivery path does not call this formatter.. Source: production/agent/formatters.py

g.title: Agent and guardrail prompts
g.desc: Prompt constants supply instructions for the three runtime agents and two guardrail agents.. Purpose: Prompt constants supply instructions for the three runtime agents and two guardrail agents.. How it works: customer_success_agent imports the triage, support and escalation constants; guardrails imports the input and output guardrail constants.. Evidence: production/agent/prompts.py: TRIAGE_AGENT_PROMPT, SUPPORT_AGENT_PROMPT, ESCALATION_AGENT_PROMPT; production/agent/prompts.py: INPUT_GUARDRAIL_PROMPT, OUTPUT_GUARDRAIL_PROMPT. Source: production/agent/prompts.py

g.title: Async PostgreSQL access layer
g.desc: Manages connection pools and shared customer, conversation, ticket, message and escalation operations.. Purpose: Manages connection pools and shared customer, conversation, ticket, message and escalation operations.. How it works: get_db_pool keeps one asyncpg pool per event loop with min_size 2 and max_size 10. Helper functions execute CRM SQL; API routes, tools and workers also issue direct SQL through the pool.. Evidence: production/database/queries.py: get_db_pool, get_or_create_customer, get_or_create_customer_by_phone; production/database/queries.py: get_or_create_conversation, create_ticket, store_message, create_escalation, get_system_stats. Source: production/database/queries.py

g.title: PostgreSQL CRM
g.desc: Relational CRM stores customer identities, conversations, messages, tickets, sentiment, escalations and channel settings.. Purpose: Relational CRM stores customer identities, conversations, messages, tickets, sentiment, escalations and channel settings.. How it works: DDL declares ten domain tables plus schema_migrations, 29 explicit indexes, pgcrypto and vector extensions. Kubernetes and Compose use pgvector PostgreSQL 16 with persistent data storage.. Evidence: production/database/schema.sql: CREATE TABLE, CREATE INDEX, pgcrypto, vector; production/k8s/03-postgres.yaml: postgres Deployment, postgres-pvc; production/docker-compose.yml: db, pgdata. Source: production/database/schema.sql

g.title: Knowledge-base table
g.desc: Product documentation records used by the support agent's retrieval tool.. Purpose: Product documentation records used by the support agent's retrieval tool.. How it works: knowledge_base defines title, content, category and vector embedding fields with a vector index. The implemented search tool performs text ILIKE matching and returns up to five results.. Evidence: production/database/schema.sql: knowledge_base, idx_knowledge_embedding; production/agent/tools.py: search_knowledge_base. Uncertainty: The implemented retrieval query uses text matching; embedding fields are not used by this query.. Source: production/database/schema.sql

g.title: Agent metrics table
g.desc: Persists per-message processing durations and periodically computed summaries.. Purpose: Persists per-message processing durations and periodically computed summaries.. How it works: agent_metrics holds metric name/value, channel, dimensions and recorded timestamp. The message worker writes message_processed; the metrics collector writes response-time, rate, queue, throughput and sentiment summaries.. Evidence: production/database/schema.sql: agent_metrics; production/workers/message_processor.py: _record_metrics; production/workers/metrics_collector.py: write_summary_metrics. Source: production/database/schema.sql

g.title: Metrics aggregation worker
g.desc: Independent scheduled loop computes database metrics and logs threshold alerts.. Purpose: Independent scheduled loop computes database metrics and logs threshold alerts.. How it works: The default interval is 60 seconds. SQL aggregates processing latency, escalation/resolution rates, sentiment, unresponded queue depth and throughput, then writes summaries back to agent_metrics.. Evidence: production/workers/metrics_collector.py: COLLECTION_INTERVAL, collect_cycle, run_loop, check_alerts; production/k8s/06b-deployment-metrics.yaml: workers/metrics_collector.py. Uncertainty: Alert output is logging; an external monitoring or notification integration is not evidenced.. Source: production/workers/metrics_collector.py

g.title: Configured OpenAI-compatible LLM
g.desc: Model endpoint used by production triage, support, escalation and guardrail runs.. Purpose: Model endpoint used by production triage, support, escalation and guardrail runs.. How it works: _setup_model constructs AsyncOpenAI and OpenAIChatCompletionsModel from environment configuration. Guardrails creates a similarly configured client for safety checks.. Evidence: production/agent/customer_success_agent.py: _setup_model, _client, _model; production/agent/guardrails.py: _get_model_config. Uncertainty: Provider and model are selected through environment configuration.. Source: production/agent/customer_success_agent.py

g.title: Gmail API
g.desc: External mail service for message listing, history retrieval, watches and replies.. Purpose: External mail service for message listing, history retrieval, watches and replies.. How it works: The adapter invokes users.messages, users.history, users.watch and MIME message sending via the Google API client.. Evidence: production/channels/gmail_handler.py: authenticate, poll_new_emails, process_notification, start_watch, send_reply. Source: production/channels/gmail_handler.py

g.title: Gmail Pub/Sub notifications
g.desc: Configured Pub/Sub topic is the destination requested by the Gmail inbox watch.. Purpose: Configured Pub/Sub topic is the destination requested by the Gmail inbox watch.. How it works: start_watch passes the configured topicName to Gmail. The API defines /webhooks/gmail to call process_notification.. Evidence: production/channels/gmail_handler.py: PUBSUB_TOPIC, start_watch; production/api/main.py: gmail_webhook. g.title: Twilio WhatsApp API
g.desc: External WhatsApp integration for incoming webhooks, polling and reply delivery.. Purpose: External WhatsApp integration for incoming webhooks, polling and reply delivery.. How it works: Twilio Client messages.list retrieves inbound messages and messages.create sends replies. The API exposes incoming-message and delivery-status webhook endpoints.. Evidence: production/channels/whatsapp_handler.py: client, poll_new_messages, send_message; production/api/main.py: whatsapp_webhook, whatsapp_status_webhook. Uncertainty: The webhook delivery edge is inferred from the Twilio adapter and the receiving API routes.. Source: production/channels/whatsapp_handler.py

g.title: Kubernetes workload definitions
g.desc: Manifests define separately scaled API, message worker, metrics worker, form frontend and data services.. Purpose: Manifests define separately scaled API, message worker, metrics worker, form frontend and data services.. How it works: Declarations specify API and worker replicas 3 each, metrics and webform replicas 1 each, plus PostgreSQL, Kafka and ZooKeeper. API and workers share the Python image but use different commands.. Evidence: production/k8s/05-deployment-api.yaml: fte-api; production/k8s/06-deployment-worker.yaml: fte-message-processor; production/k8s/06b-deployment-metrics.yaml: fte-metrics-collector; production/k8s/07-deployment-webform.yaml: fte-webform; production/k8s/03-postgres.yaml: postgres, postgres-pvc; production/k8s/04-kafka.yaml: kafka, zookeeper. g.aria-label: NGINX ingress and API Service, Service
g.title: NGINX ingress and API Service
g.desc: Declared external ingress forwards requests through a ClusterIP Service to API pods.. Purpose: Declared external ingress forwards requests through a ClusterIP Service to API pods.. How it works: The / prefix ingress targets customer-success-fte service port 80. Its selector matches API pods and forwards to container port 8000; TLS annotations and a TLS secret reference are present.. Evidence: production/k8s/09-ingress.yaml: Ingress backend; production/k8s/08-service.yaml: selector, port 80, targetPort 8000; production/k8s/05-deployment-api.yaml: API pod labels. g.aria-label: API and worker CPU autoscaling, Infrastructure
g.title: API and worker CPU autoscaling
g.desc: Two HPAs declare independent CPU-based replica ranges for API and message workers.. Purpose: Two HPAs declare independent CPU-based replica ranges for API and message workers.. How it works: fte-api-hpa targets 3 to 20 API replicas; fte-worker-hpa targets 3 to 30 worker replicas. Both target 70 percent average CPU utilization.. Evidence: production/k8s/10-hpa.yaml: fte-api-hpa, fte-worker-hpa. Source: production/k8s/10-hpa.yaml

g.title: ZooKeeper
g.desc: Coordination service declared for the repository's Kafka deployment.. Purpose: Coordination service declared for the repository's Kafka deployment.. How it works: Kubernetes exposes a ZooKeeper deployment and service on 2181; the Kafka container's KAFKA_ZOOKEEPER_CONNECT refers to it. Compose also declares a ZooKeeper service.. Evidence: production/k8s/04-kafka.yaml: zookeeper Deployment, Service, KAFKA_ZOOKEEPER_CONNECT; production/docker-compose.yml: zookeeper. Source: production/k8s/04-kafka.yaml

g.title: Docker Compose development stack
g.desc: Local stack declares PostgreSQL, ZooKeeper, Kafka and the FastAPI service.. Purpose: Local stack declares PostgreSQL, ZooKeeper, Kafka and the FastAPI service.. How it works: The db service mounts schema.sql for first initialization and a pgdata volume; the API builds the Python Dockerfile and depends on data services.. Evidence: production/docker-compose.yml: db, zookeeper, kafka, api, pgdata; production/Dockerfile: API container command. Uncertainty: Compose does not declare message-worker, metrics-worker or frontend services; their separate launch is required for the full flow.. Source: production/docker-compose.yml

g.aria-label: Python and Next.js container builds, File
g.title: Python and Next.js container builds
g.desc: Docker definitions build the API/worker runtime and the standalone Next.js frontend.. Purpose: Docker definitions build the API/worker runtime and the standalone Next.js frontend.. How it works: The Python 3.13 image installs with uv and defaults to Uvicorn. Kubernetes overrides its command for worker processes. The Node 22 multi-stage build embeds NEXT_PUBLIC_API_URL and serves standalone server.js..
